description_summary: 12-month unduplicated student headcounts broken down by student level, degree/certificate-seeking status, attendance status, student category, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYALEV; undergraduate seeking students are further identified as first-time, transfer-in, or continuing, and undergraduate attendance status distinguishes full-time from part-time. The table includes both undergraduate and graduate students, with the expanded undergraduate attendance and student-category detail available for 2019-20 and later.

12-month unduplicated student headcounts broken down by student level and distance-education status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYDLEV, with separate counts for students enrolled exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, and in no distance education; the table covers both undergraduate and graduate students.

12-month instructional activity totals broken down by undergraduate versus graduate level and by credit-hour and/or contact-hour activity. The grain is the institution (UNITID) by student level and instructional-activity type; these are activity measures rather than unduplicated student headcounts and are used to derive 12-month FTE enrollment.

Academic library characteristics, collections, expenditures, services, and full-time-equivalent library staff counts for fiscal year 2020, reported at the institution/library level. Applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available only for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000. Collection measures include physical and electronic serials, collected since fiscal year 2016–17.

For Fall 2020, this institution-level table contains undergraduate admission considerations, applicant counts, admissions, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT score fields for entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students. It applies to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time students; SAT and ACT scores are reported only by institutions that require those tests for admission. Each record is unique to an institution, with separate fields for the consideration practices and applicant, admitted, enrolled, and test-score measures.

Awards and degrees conferred by 6-digit 2020 CIPCODE, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; it contains award totals and demographic subtotals. Beginning in 2019-20, the former less-than-1-year certificate level is split into certificates of less than 12 weeks and certificates of at least 12 weeks but less than 1 year.

Students receiving any degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. Each institution has one record uniquely identified by UNITID, with total, male, female, and race/ethnicity-specific student counts; it is not broken out by program or award level.

Students receiving degrees or certificates broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age group. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age counts cover under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age cannot be combined in the same count. Beginning in 2019-20, the less-than-1-year certificate level is split into certificates of less than 12 weeks and certificates of at least 12 weeks but less than 1 year.

Programs offered and their distance-education availability, broken down by award level and 2020 CIPCODE. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: six-digit CIP records indicate which award levels are offered and whether all or some programs at each level can be completed entirely by distance education; two-digit CIP records summarize the number of six-digit CIP codes in the group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals. More detailed distance-education categories and the split of less-than-1-year certificates into less than 12 weeks and at least 12 weeks but less than 1 year begin in 2019-20.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL and includes total, men’s, and women’s counts overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL and includes total, men’s, and women’s counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFDELEV and includes total enrollment plus counts enrolled exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, or in none; exclusive-distance counts are further broken down by geographic location relative to the institution.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age enrollments are optional for institutions to report in even-numbered years, so 2020 (even) may have data only for institutions that reported it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school in the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence enrollments are optional for institutions to report in odd-numbered years, so 2020 (even) has no data under this collection rule.

Fall enrollment counts for selected major fields—Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. This table is restricted to four-year institutions; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field, attendance status, and EFCIPLEV.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, applicable only to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institution-level finance records for public institutions using GASB 34/35, with one record per institution, covering revenues, functional and natural-classification expenditures, endowments, assets, liabilities, and financial health measures. Beginning in fiscal year 2020, scholarship and fellowship discounts and allowances are reported by source, and more detailed endowment data are available; detailed expenditure categories discontinued after fiscal year 2015 are absent.

Institution-level finance records for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, with one record per institution, covering revenues, functional and natural-classification expenditures, endowments, assets, liabilities, and financial health measures. Beginning in fiscal year 2020, scholarship and fellowship discounts and allowances are reported by source, and more detailed endowment data are available; detailed expenditure categories discontinued after fiscal year 2015 are absent.

Institution-level finance records for private for-profit FASB institutions, with one record per institution, covering revenues, functional and natural-classification expenditures, assets, liabilities, and financial health measures. This form does not include the endowment measures available in the GASB and private-not-for-profit/public-FASB forms; beginning in fiscal year 2020, scholarship and fellowship discounts and allowances are reported by source, while detailed expenditure categories discontinued after fiscal year 2015 remain absent.

Graduation outcomes within 200% of normal time for four-year institutions’ 2012 cohorts and less-than-4-year institutions’ 2016 cohorts. Records are institution-level cohort-status records identified by UNITID and GRTYPE; four-year data are for bachelor’s-degree seekers, while less-than-4-year data cover students completing any degree or certificate. This component is reported in even-numbered years, so 2020 (even) has data.

Graduation outcomes within 150% of normal time for four-year institutions’ 2014 cohorts and two-year institutions’ 2017 cohorts, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and GRTYPE; the table covers bachelor’s-degree seekers and other degree/certificate seekers at four-year institutions and the applicable full-time, first-time cohort at two-year institutions. Two-year institutions do not have 100%-of-normal-time completion counts by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation outcomes within 150% of normal time for the 2017 cohort at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment, completion at 100% or 150% of normal time, and transfers out. Records are institution-level cohort-status records identified by UNITID and GRTYPE, with no four-year or two-year institution populations in this table.

Graduation outcomes within 150% of normal time for financial-aid subcohorts at four-year, two-year, and less-than-2-year institutions: Pell Grant recipients; subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell; and students who received neither. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and PSGRTYPE; four-year records use the 2014 cohort, while two-year and less-than-2-year records use the 2017 cohort. This optional component is reported in even-numbered years, so 2020 (even) has data.

Fall staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty and tenure status, and contract length for non-tenure-track staff. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and EAPCAT, which combines the occupational category and tenure-status classification; multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available beginning in 2016.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with contract-length detail for non-tenure-track staff. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines FACSTAT and academic rank (ARANK); multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available beginning in 2016. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years and mandatory in odd-numbered years beginning in 2001, but became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2020 (even) has data.

Full-time new-hire counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender; instructional new hires also have faculty/tenure-status and, beginning in 2016, contract-length detail. New hires are permanent full-time hires made for the first time or after a break in service during November 1, 2019 through October 31, 2020, and each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and SNHCAT, the primary-occupation and instructional faculty/tenure classification. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years and mandatory in odd-numbered years beginning in 2001, but became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2020 (even) has data.

Payroll staff counts as of November 1, broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- or part-time status. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and STAFFCAT, the occupational-category and full-/part-time classification. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years and mandatory in odd-numbered years beginning in 2001, but became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2020 (even) has data.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty and tenure status, and contract length for non-tenure-track staff. Each record is uniquely defined by UNITID and FACSTAT, the faculty-and-tenure-status classification; multi-year and indefinite contract categories are available beginning in 2016.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated 9-month salary measures for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. Records are defined by UNITID and academic rank (ARANK); staff working fewer than 9 months have counts but no salary data.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff, organized by occupational category in institution-by-occupation records.

Institution-submitted custom comparison-group membership for the 2021 Data Feedback Report, linking a reporting institution to each comparison institution by the reporting institution’s UNITID and the comparison institution’s IPEDS ID. The comparison institution’s name and state are also provided.

Survey-component response and applicability records for each institution, keyed by UNITID and survey component. It distinguishes reported, nonrespondent/imputed, and inapplicable components and identifies parent/child or multiple-campus reporting and revised submissions.

Institution directory and classification information for each institution, keyed by UNITID. It includes names and contact or web information, active status, Title IV participation, control and institutional level, highest award or degree offered, and Carnegie classifications.

Institution-level offerings, organization, admissions, services, and affiliations, keyed by UNITID. It covers award-level and program offerings, control and affiliation, special learning opportunities, open-admission policy, distance-education offerings, library services, and athletic associations; from 2020-21 onward, less-than-one-year certificates are separated into less-than-12-weeks and at-least-12-weeks-but-less-than-one-year categories.

Student charges for full academic-year programs, keyed by UNITID, for institutions whose primarily academic credit-hour programs use a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar. It distinguishes full-time undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees, part-time undergraduate and graduate per-credit-hour charges, professional-practice doctoral charges, and published attendance costs for full-time first-time undergraduates.

Student charges for vocational or occupational programs measured in clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, keyed by UNITID and reported program slot. It provides the number of programs, attendance costs for the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books-and-supplies charges for up to five additional programs; charges are for the full length of each program rather than an academic year.
An institution’s mission statement or its web address, keyed by UNITID. This table contains one institution-level mission record rather than offerings, charges, or response-status data.

Award and enrollment outcomes for degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who entered during July 1, 2012–June 30, 2013, measured at four, six, and eight years as of August 31, 2016, August 31, 2018, and August 31, 2020. It covers four entering groups—first-time full-time, first-time part-time, non-first-time full-time, and non-first-time part-time—each split into Pell recipients and non-Pell recipients; all such entering students at degree-granting institutions are assigned to one subcohort. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort (OMCHRT), and contains adjusted cohort size plus counts and percentages completing or still enrolled.

Student financial aid recipients and aid dollars broken down by student population and aid source. The reporting grain is institution × population × aid type: full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates are reported for federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loan categories, while all undergraduates are reported for total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans; each cell includes recipient counts and total and average aid amounts.

Average net price and its underlying financial-aid measures for two populations: full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving grant or scholarship aid, and those receiving Title IV federal aid. The reporting grain is institution × population; at public institutions, both populations are restricted to students paying the in-district or in-state tuition rate.

Military and veteran benefit recipients and benefit dollars broken down by student level and benefit program. The reporting grain is institution × undergraduate/graduate level × benefit type, covering Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits and Department of Defense Tuition Assistance; this file is collected only in odd-numbered years, so 2020 (even) has no data.
